first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and two independent inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) converge on onboarding/signup simplification as the lever that moves both, so it is the best single-slot candidate on the surface. But the objective is sustainable long-term QUALIFIED revenue, and the two memories that most need auditing are exactly the ones whose stated wins may be measured on the wrong metric. memory_31 claims a lift from 'cutting required fields at signup' — that is a top-of-funnel activation metric, and stripping signup fields plausibly degrades the firmographic data used to route enterprise prospects into the demo-request path that memory_44 says produces the better pipeline quality. So the recorded activation win could coexist with a silent loss in qualified pipeline; I need the original record to see whether revenue/pipeline quality was even tracked, and over what horizon. memory_73 is the other audit target because competitive price pressure makes promotional pricing the tempting reflex, and 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is precisely the phrasing that can hide discount-acquired, low-retention SMB cohorts — a short-window win that is negative against a long-term qualified-revenue objective. I am verifying the memory behind my intended action and the memory behind my strongest alternative, rather than spending budget confirming what I already plan to do. I did not verify memory_86 because it is directionally corroborated by memory_31 and is the weaker of the pair to spend budget on; if memory_31's record turns out to be sound but narrow, memory_86 becomes the load-bearing evidence and I should revisit. All of these memories are consolidated summaries 15-64 days old with sources archived, and none of them were formed under the current competitor's entry pricing, so their transportability to day 76 conditions is itself uncertain. Hence a small guarded test, not a broad rollout: I will hold the enterprise-relevant qualifying fields (or make them progressive/post-signup) rather than cutting indiscriminately, and instrument downstream qualified pipeline and retention, not just completion and week-one activation. If verification shows memory_31 cut qualification-bearing fields and never measured downstream, I will narrow to activation_messaging (memory_91), which lifts week-one engagement without touching the qualification surface. Notably, I am not treating the competitor's pricing move as an argument for matching it; responding to price pressure with margin-eroding discounts is the action most likely to book revenue that does not survive the year.
